Guess first. The box score is the check.

## NBA Individual Power Ratings

In game statistics

* STEALS 
 
* TURNOVERS - Turnover occurs when a team loses possession of the ball to the opposing team before a player takes a shot at their team's basket.  
https://www.youtube.com/shorts/I4MDXOWrUmk
* REBOUNDS
  1. OFFENSIVE REBOUNDS - An offensive rebound occurs when offensive players regain possession of the ball after a missed shot.
  2. DEFENSIVE REBOUNDS -  Defensive rebounds occur when defensive players gain possession of the ball after an offensive player misses the shot.
* BLOCKS - Block occurs when a defensive player legally deflects a field goal attempt from an offensive player to prevent a score.
* FOULS
  1. PERSONAL FOULS
  2. FLAGRANT FOULS
  3. TECHINCAL FOULS


## NBA Individual Power Ratings

### Dataset: `nba_players`

Season box scores from Basketball-Reference, through 2024-25. One row is one player-season. `Year` is the season ending year, so 2025 is 2024-25.

```{r, include = F}
data("nba_players")
stopifnot(max(nba_players$Year, na.rm = TRUE) >= 2025)
nba_players <- nba_players %>%
  filter(Year > 1997, Year <= 2025)
```

* Identity: `Year`, `Player`, `Pos`, `Tm`
* Time: `G` games, `GS` starts, `MP` minutes
* Defense: `STL`, `TOV`, `DRB`, `BLK`, `PF`
* Offense: `PTS`, `AST`, `ORB`, `FG`/`FGA`, `X3P`/`X3PA`, `FT`/`FTA`
* Rates end with a dot: `FG.` is field-goal percentage

```{r, include=FALSE}
nba_players <- nba_players %>%
  select(Year, Player, Pos, Tm,
         G, GS, MP, STL, TOV, ORB, DRB, PF, BLK, PTS, AST,
         FT, FTA, FG, FGA, X3P, X3PA, X2P, X2PA, ORB., DRB.,
         TRB., AST., STL., BLK., TOV., FG., X3P., FT.,) %>%
  arrange(Player, Year)
```

## NBA Individual Power Ratings

Counting totals is not a rating.

* A total grows when a player stays on the floor
* Points and minutes move together for that reason
* Dividing by minutes asks what he did per minute

The next slides use one season of totals on purpose, so the trap is visible. They are not a five-year average, and they are not a success rate.

## NBA Individual Power Ratings

Let's start with defending attributes.

Successful actions, when defending  

* STEALS
* BLOCKS
* DEFENSIVE REBOUNDS

Non Successful actions, when defending  


* PERSONAL FOULS
* TURNOVER

## NBA Individual Power Ratings

Let's calculate the difference between the cumulative success actions and cumulative failure actions.  
\tiny
```{r}
nba_players_defence <- nba_players %>%
  arrange(Player, Year) %>% 
  filter(Pos %in% c('SF','PG')) %>%
  group_by(Player) %>%
  mutate(STL_TOV = STL - TOV,
         STL_PF = STL - PF,
         DRB_TOV = DRB - TOV,
         BLK_TOV = BLK - TOV,
         BLK_PF = BLK - PF) %>%
  drop_na(STL_TOV, STL_PF, DRB_TOV, BLK_TOV, BLK_PF, MP) %>%
  ungroup()
```

## NBA Individual Power Ratings

Let's check if the metrics are correlated to the amount of time the players spent on the field.

```{r}
cor_with_MP <- function(x){
  return(cor(x, nba_players_defence$MP))
}

nba_players_defence %>%
  select(STL_TOV, STL_PF, DRB_TOV, BLK_TOV, BLK_PF) %>%
  apply(2,cor_with_MP)
```



## NBA Individual Power Ratings

The metric with the highest positive correlation rate is the Seasonal difference between
the seasonal number of defensive rebounds made and number of turnovers made.  

\tiny
```{r, out.height="60%", fig.align="center"}
ggplot(nba_players_defence, aes(x = DRB_TOV, y = (MP))) + 
  geom_point() + 
  ggtitle("Number of Minutes played vs Seasonal defensive rating(DRB - TOV)") + 
  xlab("Seasonal Defensive Rating(DRB - TOV)") + 
  ylab("Minutes played")
```

## NBA Individual Power Ratings

The metric with the highest negative correlation is blocks minus personal fouls.  

\tiny
```{r, out.height="60%",fig.align="center"}
ggplot(nba_players_defence, aes(x = BLK_PF, y = (MP))) + 
  geom_point() + 
  ggtitle("Number of Minutes played vs Seasonal defensive rating(BLK - PF)") + 
  xlab("Seasonal Defensive Rating(BLK - PF)") + 
  ylab("Minutes played")
```

## NBA Individual Power Ratings

Let's fit a model with the defensive power ratings.  

\tiny
```{r}
summary(lm(MP ~ (STL_TOV + STL_PF + DRB_TOV + BLK_PF ), data = nba_players_defence))
```


## NBA Individual Power Ratings

Read the defense regression as playing time, not as a cause.

* Season totals grow with minutes, so the correlations are expected
* More rebounds do not, by themselves, "earn" more minutes
* A rating has to divide by minutes before it ranks players


## NBA Individual Power Ratings

For the attacking attributes we will calculate the difference between the attempts made for successful actions and actual successful actions.

Successful actions, when attacking  

* FIELD GOALS
* 3 POINT GOALS
* FREE THROWS
* OFFENSIVE REBOUNDS
* POINTS SCORED
* ASSISTS MADE

Non Successful actions, when attacking  

* FIELD GOALS ATTEMPTS
* 3 POINT ATTEMPTS
* FREE THROW ATTEMPTS

## NBA Individual Power Ratings


```{r}
nba_players_offense <- nba_players %>%
  arrange(Player, Year)  %>% 
  group_by(Player) %>%
  mutate(FGA_FG = FGA - FG,
         X3PA_X3P = X3PA - X3P,
         FTA_FT = FTA - FT) %>%
  drop_na(FGA_FG, X3PA_X3P, FTA_FT, AST, PTS, MP) %>%
  ungroup()
```

Let's check if the Seasonal metrics are correlated to the amount of time the players spent on the field.

```{r}
cor_with_MP <- function(x){
  return(cor(x, nba_players_offense$MP))
}

nba_players_offense %>%
  select(FGA_FG, X3PA_X3P, FTA_FT, AST, PTS) %>%
  apply(2,cor_with_MP)
```

## NBA Individual Power Ratings

2024-25 scoring list. Second in points: is he second per minute?

Vote before the tables. Anthony Edwards plays the most minutes of this group.

```{r, echo=FALSE}
rate_2025 <- nba_players %>%
  filter(Year == 2025, MP > 0) %>%
  mutate(PTS36 = PTS / MP * 36)

by_points <- rate_2025 %>%
  filter(MP > 500) %>%
  arrange(desc(PTS)) %>%
  transmute(Player, Pos, Tm, MP = round(MP), PTS, PTS36 = round(PTS36, 1)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5)

by_rate <- rate_2025 %>%
  filter(MP > 1500) %>%
  arrange(desc(PTS36)) %>%
  transmute(Player, Pos, Tm, MP = round(MP), PTS, PTS36 = round(PTS36, 1)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 5)
```

summary(lm(MP ~ (PTS + AST + FGA_FG + X3PA_X3P + FTA_FT), data = nba_players_offense))

## NBA Individual Power Ratings

The offense regression has the same trap.

* Scoring more is not what puts a player on the floor
* Minutes produce points, assists, and missed shots
* Use the per-36 table, not this coefficient, when you rank scorers


# Plus/Minus

## Plus/Minus


### The concept

Plus-minus measures the point differential for the team when the player is on the court,  

Point differential is the difference in the points scored for and the points scored against the team.  

The Montreal Canadiens tracked plus/minus in the 1950s. The NHL made it official for 1967-68. A goal total ignores the goals against while that player was on the ice.

## One stint, by hand

Home scores 2. Away scores 0. Durant is at home.

* Each home player, including Durant: +2
* Each away player: -2
* A player who is sitting: 0 for this stint

Season plus/minus is the sum of the stints he actually played.

## Plus/minus for NBA

This file is the 2011-12 lockout season, from 25 December 2011 to 26 April 2012.

* One row is a stint: the same ten players stay on the floor
* Coverage is uneven. New Jersey has 28 games in the file, Memphis has 66
* The Finals are not in the file. That June, Miami beat Oklahoma City
* The number you compute is for these stints, not the official season total

```{r, echo=F}
data(nba12, package = "SportsAnalytics270")
data(nba12p, package = "SportsAnalytics270")
data(nba5, package = "SportsAnalytics270")
library(SportsAnalytics270)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(VGAM)
library(zoo)
library(tidyr)

name_coeffs <- function(coeff, info) {
  # lm writes 714 as `714` or X714; undo both before joining nba12p
  ids <- sub("^X", "", gsub("`", "", names(coeff)))
  key <- info %>%
    mutate(PlayerID = as.character(PlayerID)) %>%
    select(PlayerID, PlayerTrueName)
  joined <- left_join(
    data.frame(id = ids, stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
    key,
    by = c("id" = "PlayerID")
  )
  labels <- ifelse(
    is.na(joined$PlayerTrueName),
    joined$id,
    as.character(joined$PlayerTrueName)
  )
  stats::setNames(as.numeric(coeff), labels)
}

player_pm <- function(stints, player_id) {
  player_id <- as.character(player_id)
  home_cols <- paste0("HomePlayer", 1:5, "ID")
  away_cols <- paste0("AwayPlayer", 1:5, "ID")
  on_home <- Reduce(`|`, lapply(home_cols, function(col) as.character(stints[[col]]) == player_id))
  on_away <- Reduce(`|`, lapply(away_cols, function(col) as.character(stints[[col]]) == player_id))
  margin <- stints$PointsScoredHome - stints$PointsScoredAway
  sum(margin[on_home]) - sum(margin[on_away])
}

md_date <- function(d) {
  paste(month.abb[as.integer(format(d, "%m"))], as.integer(format(d, "%d")))
}

pm_slide_plot <- function(data, y, title, ylab) {
  ticks <- c(1, 21, 41, nrow(data))
  ggplot(data, aes(x = Game, y = .data[[y]])) +
    geom_col() +
    scale_x_continuous(
      breaks = ticks,
      labels = md_date(data$Date[ticks]),
      expand = expansion(mult = c(0.04, 0.10))
    ) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    labs(x = "Game date", y = ylab, title = title) +
    theme(
      plot.margin = margin(6, 18, 4, 6),
      axis.text.x = element_text(hjust = c(0, 0.5, 0.5, 1))
    )
}

apm_rank <- function(coeff, who) {
  x <- coeff[names(coeff) != "(Intercept)"]
  i <- match(who, names(x))
  data.frame(Player = who, APM = unname(x[i]), rank = i)
}
```

## The stint file: `nba12`

25,300 rows. One row is one stretch of 2011-12 with the same ten players on the floor.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
data(nba12, package = "SportsAnalytics270")
```

* Game: `GameID`, `Date`, `AwayT`, `HomeT`
* Who is on the floor: `HomePlayer1Name` to `HomePlayer5Name`, same for away, and matching `...ID` columns
* Scoring: `PointsScoredHome`, `PointsScoredAway`
* Length: `ElapsedSecs`, `PossessionsHome`, `PossessionsAway`

## Three stints, Christmas, Knicks at home

Boston is away. `PossessionsHome` counts New York trips; `PossessionsAway` counts Boston trips.

\tiny
```{r, echo=FALSE}
stint_ex <- nba12 %>%
  filter(GameID == "20111225BOSNYK") %>%
  select(HomeT, AwayT, PointsScoredHome, PointsScoredAway,
         PossessionsHome, PossessionsAway)
stint_rows <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::filter(stint_ex, PossessionsHome == 0, PossessionsAway == 1) %>% slice(1),
  dplyr::filter(stint_ex, PossessionsHome == 1, PossessionsAway == 0) %>% slice(1),
  dplyr::filter(stint_ex, PossessionsHome == 1, PossessionsAway == 1,
                PointsScoredHome == 2, PointsScoredAway == 0) %>% slice(1)
)
knitr::kable(stint_rows, format = "simple")
```

* Row 1. `PossessionsHome = 0`: New York did not have the ball. Boston did, and scored 2.
* Row 2. `PossessionsHome = 1`: New York had the ball once. Boston had 0 possessions.
* Row 3. Both equal 1: each team had one trip. New York scored 2, Boston scored 0.

## The player file: `nba12p`

One row is one player in that stint file. Use it to attach names and minutes to player IDs.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
data(nba12p, package = "SportsAnalytics270")
```

* `PlayerID` matches the ID columns in `nba12`
* `PlayerTrueName`, `PlayerTeams`
* `SimpleMin`: minutes in these stints, not necessarily the official season total

## Four players from `nba12p`

`PlayerID` 714 is Durant. That is the number in the `nba12` lineup columns.

\tiny
```{r}
nba12p %>%
  filter(PlayerTrueName %in% c("Durant, Kevin", "James, LeBron",
                               "Westbrook, Russell", "Benson, Keith")) %>%
  select(PlayerID, PlayerTrueName, PlayerTeams, SimpleMin)
```

## Oklahoma City from `nba12`

`GameID` is the date plus the two team codes, for example `20111225ORLOKC`. Keep the rows that contain `OKC`.

\tiny
```{r}
okc <- nba12 %>%
  filter(grepl("OKC", GameID, fixed = TRUE))
nrow(okc)
okc %>%
  select(GameID, Date, HomeT, AwayT) %>%
  slice(1:3)
```

1,716 stints, from Thunder games only.

## Stint plus/minus

Same scoring columns as in `nba12`. Home margin is points scored minus points allowed. Away margin is the opposite.

\tiny
```{r}
okc <- okc %>%
  mutate(
    Home_PM = PointsScoredHome - PointsScoredAway,
    Away_PM = -Home_PM
  )
okc %>%
  filter(PointsScoredHome + PointsScoredAway > 0) %>%
  select(HomeT, AwayT, PointsScoredHome, PointsScoredAway, Home_PM, Away_PM) %>%
  slice(1:3)
```

First scoring stint: OKC at home, 18-18, so both margins are 0. A later 2-0 stint would be `Home_PM = 2`.

## Is Durant on the floor?

Paste all five names, then search the string. Still the OKC rows, not the full `nba12` file.

\tiny
```{r}
okc <- okc %>%
  mutate(
    line_h = paste(HomePlayer1Name, HomePlayer2Name, HomePlayer3Name,
                   HomePlayer4Name, HomePlayer5Name, sep = ","),
    line_a = paste(AwayPlayer1Name, AwayPlayer2Name, AwayPlayer3Name,
                   AwayPlayer4Name, AwayPlayer5Name, sep = ","),
    D_H = grepl("Durant", line_h, fixed = TRUE),
    D_A = grepl("Durant", line_a, fixed = TRUE)
  )
```

## Is Durant on the floor?

Christmas, one stint. These are the five names that went into `line_h` and `line_a`.

\tiny
```{r, echo=FALSE}
one <- okc %>%
  filter(GameID == "20111225ORLOKC") %>%
  slice(1)
knitr::kable(
  one %>% transmute(
    Home = HomeT, H1 = HomePlayer1Name, H2 = HomePlayer2Name,
    H3 = HomePlayer3Name, H4 = HomePlayer4Name, H5 = HomePlayer5Name,
    D_H
  ),
  format = "simple"
)
knitr::kable(
  one %>% transmute(
    Away = AwayT, A1 = AwayPlayer1Name, A2 = AwayPlayer2Name,
    A3 = AwayPlayer3Name, A4 = AwayPlayer4Name, A5 = AwayPlayer5Name,
    D_A
  ),
  format = "simple"
)
```

* `D_H = TRUE`: H3 is Durant, so `"Durant"` is in `line_h`
* `D_A = FALSE`: Durant is not in Orlando's five, so this stint uses `Home_PM`

## Plus/minus for NBA

Durant's season plus/minus in this file: add the stint margin when he is on the floor.

```{r tidy=F}
# D_H / D_A: Durant is in the home or away five for that stint
durant_season <- sum(okc$Home_PM[okc$D_H]) + sum(okc$Away_PM[okc$D_A])
durant_season
```

This is his plus/minus over the stints in this file, not the official 2011-12 total.

## Plus/minus for NBA

LeBron needs a player id. Three players in this file have the last name James.

```{r}
# nba12p has three players named James; match the full name
lebron_id <- nba12p$PlayerID[nba12p$PlayerTrueName == "James, LeBron"]
lebron_season <- player_pm(nba12, lebron_id)
c(Durant = durant_season, LeBron = lebron_season)
```

## Plus/minus for NBA

One number per Oklahoma City game, in date order.

\tiny
```{r tidy=F}
durant_pm <- okc %>%
  # this stint: home margin if Durant is home, away margin if he is away
  mutate(PM = ifelse(D_H, Home_PM, ifelse(D_A, Away_PM, 0))) %>%
  group_by(GameID) %>%
  summarise(
    PM = sum(PM),  # add the stints in that game
    Date = as.Date(as.character(min(Date)), format = "%Y%m%d"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(Date) %>%
  mutate(Game = row_number())  # 1, 2, 3... for the bar chart
```

## Plus/minus for NBA

\tiny
```{r}
head(durant_pm, n=5)
```



## Plus/minus for NBA

Each bar is one Oklahoma City game in this file, in date order.

```{r, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7.4, fig.height=3.05, out.width="\\linewidth", fig.align="center"}
pm_slide_plot(durant_pm, "PM", "Kevin Durant, plus/minus by game", "Plus/minus")
```

## On court and off court +/\- and Roland’s rating

The on court +/\- number represents the team's net points with the player on the floor per 48 minutes, while the off court number is the team's net with the player off the floor per 48 minutes.  

The Roland Rating is the difference between the two, with a positive number indicating the team has played better with the player than without.  

## OKC's margin, and whether Durant played

OKC is home in some rows and away in others. `OKC_PM` is always Thunder points minus opponent points. `D_PM` is TRUE if Durant was in either five.

\tiny
```{r}
okc <- okc %>%
  mutate(
    OKC_PM = ifelse(AwayT == "OKC", Away_PM,
                    ifelse(HomeT == "OKC", Home_PM, 0)),
    D_PM = D_H | D_A
  )
okc %>%
  filter(OKC_PM != 0) %>%
  group_by(HomeT) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(HomeT, AwayT, D_H, D_PM, Home_PM, Away_PM, OKC_PM)
```

When OKC is home, `OKC_PM` equals `Home_PM`. When OKC is away, it equals `Away_PM`.

## Net Plus/minus for NBA

First half: one row for Durant on the floor, one row for Durant on the bench.

\tiny
```{r}
durant_long <- okc %>%
  group_by(GameID, D_PM) %>%
  summarise(
    PM = sum(OKC_PM),  # OKC margin while he is on, then while he is off
    Date = as.Date(as.character(min(Date)), format = "%Y%m%d"),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(court = ifelse(D_PM, "on", "off")) %>%
  select(GameID, Date, court, PM)
head(durant_long, 4)
```

Christmas is two rows: off $+7$, on $+1$. Not yet subtracted.

## What `pivot_wider` does

A toy game with the same two rows.

\tiny
```{r}
toy <- data.frame(
  Game = c("Christmas", "Christmas"),
  court = c("on", "off"),
  PM = c(1, 7)
)
toy
tidyr::pivot_wider(toy, names_from = court, values_from = PM)
```

`names_from = court` turns the words `"on"` and `"off"` into column names. `values_from = PM` fills those columns. Two rows become one.

## Net Plus/minus for NBA

Second half: widen, then subtract. A game with no bench stint has `off = NA` and drops out.

\tiny
```{r}
durant_net <- durant_long %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = court, values_from = PM) %>%
  mutate(NET = on - off) %>%  # Roland's rating for that game
  filter(is.finite(NET)) %>%
  arrange(Date) %>%
  mutate(Game = row_number())
```

## Net Plus/minus for NBA

Christmas: OKC was +1 with Durant on the floor and +7 with him off, so NET is $-6$.

\tiny
```{r}
head(durant_net)
```

## Plus/minus for NBA

```{r, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7.4, fig.height=3.05, out.width="\\linewidth", fig.align="center"}
pm_slide_plot(durant_net, "NET", "Kevin Durant, on-court minus off-court", "Net plus/minus")
```

## A parallel-axis plot, by hand

The x-axis is not time. It is three scales side by side. One player is three numbers, then one line.

\tiny
```{r}
toy_pc <- data.frame(
  player = rep(c("Alice", "Bob"), each = 3),
  axis = factor(
    rep(c("Speed", "Strength", "Skill"), 2),
    levels = c("Speed", "Strength", "Skill")
  ),
  rating = c(8, 4, 9,  3, 9, 5)
)
toy_pc
```

## A parallel-axis plot, by hand

`group = player` connects the three points. Alice is high on speed and skill. Bob is high on strength.

\tiny
```{r, fig.width=7, fig.height=2.5, out.width="\\linewidth", fig.align="center"}
ggplot(toy_pc, aes(axis, rating, group = player, color = player)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  ylab("Rating")
```

## Roland rating, the long table

Six Thunder games, drawn at random. Same shape as the toy: one row is one game on one axis.

\tiny
```{r}
set.seed(270)
opp_from_id <- function(id) {
  gsub("OKC", "", sub("^[0-9]+", "", as.character(id)))
}
roland_ex <- durant_net %>%
  slice_sample(n = 6) %>%
  mutate(game = paste(md_date(Date), opp_from_id(GameID)))
pc <- roland_ex %>%
  transmute(
    game,
    `Off court` = off,
    `On court` = on,
    Roland = NET
  ) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-game, names_to = "axis", values_to = "rating") %>%
  mutate(axis = factor(axis, levels = c("Off court", "On court", "Roland")))
head(pc, 6)
```

## Roland rating, parallel axes

In which game did Durant have the best performance?

\tiny
```{r, fig.width=7.4, fig.height=2.9, out.width="\\linewidth", fig.align="center"}
ggplot(pc, aes(axis, rating, group = game, color = game)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point() +
  ylab("Rating")
```

## Plus/minus, on film

Raw plus/minus in a real NBA stretch. Then we adjust it for who else is on the floor.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5WRe6SoBh3g

# Adjusted plus/minus

## Why raw plus/minus is not enough

Durant's season plus/minus credits him for every point while he is on the floor, including Westbrook's.

Adjusted plus/minus asks a different question: holding the other nine players fixed, how much does **this** player move the home margin?

Dan Rosenbaum, [82games](http://www.82games.com/comm30.htm): \(\beta_k\) is player \(k\) versus the reference, with the other players held constant.

## The regression

One row is still one stint. The outcome is that stint's home margin. Each player is a dummy.

\bcenter
$MARGIN = \beta_0 + \beta_1X_1 + \beta_2X_2 + \cdots + \beta_kX_k + \epsilon$
\ecenter

* \(MARGIN = \text{PointsScoredHome} - \text{PointsScoredAway}\)
* \(X_k = 1\) if player \(k\) is on the **home** five
* \(X_k = -1\) if player \(k\) is on the **away** five
* \(X_k = 0\) if player \(k\) is **not on the floor**
* \(\beta_0\) is home court. \(\beta_k\) is that player's adjusted plus/minus

## The same stint, as a row

Home scores 2, away scores 0, so \(MARGIN = +2\).

* Five home players, including Durant: \(X = 1\)
* Five away players: \(X = -1\)
* Everyone else that night, including Benson if he is sitting: \(X = 0\)

A season of these rows is the regression. Durant's \(\beta\) is his APM.

## Code one stint from `nba12`

Christmas, OKC at home. Same five-name idea as `D_H`, but now with player IDs.

\tiny
```{r}
one <- nba12 %>%
  filter(GameID == "20111225ORLOKC") %>%
  slice(1)
home_ids <- as.character(c(
  one$HomePlayer1ID, one$HomePlayer2ID, one$HomePlayer3ID,
  one$HomePlayer4ID, one$HomePlayer5ID
))
away_ids <- as.character(c(
  one$AwayPlayer1ID, one$AwayPlayer2ID, one$AwayPlayer3ID,
  one$AwayPlayer4ID, one$AwayPlayer5ID
))
```

## The ten IDs on the floor

Same Christmas five as before. These names built `home_ids` and `away_ids`.

\tiny
```{r, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(
  one %>% transmute(
    Home = HomeT, H1 = HomePlayer1Name, H2 = HomePlayer2Name,
    H3 = HomePlayer3Name, H4 = HomePlayer4Name, H5 = HomePlayer5Name
  ),
  format = "simple"
)
knitr::kable(
  one %>% transmute(
    Away = AwayT, A1 = AwayPlayer1Name, A2 = AwayPlayer2Name,
    A3 = AwayPlayer3Name, A4 = AwayPlayer4Name, A5 = AwayPlayer5Name
  ),
  format = "simple"
)
```

```{r}
home_ids
away_ids
```

Durant is H3, ID 714. Nelson is A1, ID 158.

## Turn an ID into 1 / -1 / 0

If the ID is in `home_ids`, code `1`. If it is in `away_ids`, code `-1`. Otherwise `0`.

\tiny
```{r}
x_code <- function(id) {
  id <- as.character(id)
  ifelse(id %in% home_ids, 1, ifelse(id %in% away_ids, -1, 0))
}
c(
  Durant = x_code(714),
  Westbrook = x_code(786),
  Nelson = x_code(158),
  Benson = x_code(1027)
)
```

Benson's ID is 1027. He is in neither five, so this stint does not move his coefficient.

## The APM table: `nba5`

That coding, for every player and every stint, is already in `SportsAnalytics270`. Rows are in the same order as `nba12`.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
data(nba5, package = "SportsAnalytics270")
```

* 25,300 rows, 474 player columns
* Cell is `1` home, `-1` away, `0` not on the floor
* Column names are player IDs. R puts an `X` in front of a name that starts with a digit, so 714 is `X714`

```{r}
dim(nba5)
head(colnames(nba5), 4)
```

## One stint in `nba5`

Same Christmas row. `nba5` should match the codes we just built from `nba12`.

\tiny
```{r}
i <- which(nba12$GameID == "20111225ORLOKC")[1]
nba5[i, c("X714", "X786", "X158", "X1027")]
```

Durant and Westbrook `1`, Nelson `-1`, Benson `0`. Same as `x_code`.

## Attach the margin from `nba12`

`nba5` has the \(X\) columns only. The outcome is still home points minus away points, from `nba12`.

\tiny
```{r}
nba5 <- data.frame(
  PM = nba12$PointsScoredHome - nba12$PointsScoredAway,
  nba5
)
nba5[i, c("PM", "X714", "X786", "X158", "X1027")]
```

Christmas, 18-18: `PM = 0`. The dummies did not change. This is one row of \(MARGIN = \beta_0 + \sum \beta_k X_k\).

## Fit the regression

`PM ~ .` means: home margin, explained by every player column.

* `X = 1`: on the home five, this `PM` is counted as his
* `X = -1`: on the away five, this `PM` is counted against him
* `X = 0`: not on the floor, this stint does not move his \(\beta\)

The coefficient is his APM, holding the other players fixed.

\tiny
```{r}
model <- lm(PM ~ ., data = nba5)
coeff <- sort(coefficients(model), decreasing = TRUE)
head(names(coeff), 4)
```

The names are still IDs, `X714` not `"Durant, Kevin"`.

## Put names on the coefficients

`name_coeffs` strips the `X`, then joins `PlayerID` in `nba12p`.

\tiny
```{r}
tiny <- c("(Intercept)" = unname(coeff["(Intercept)"]),
          X714 = unname(coeff["X714"]),
          X786 = unname(coeff["X786"]))
tiny
name_coeffs(tiny, nba12p)
coeff_all <- name_coeffs(coeff, nba12p)
```

## A slice of `summary(model)`

`summary(model)` has 475 rows. Print the Christmas-stint players, then the 95% range from `confint()`.

\tiny
```{r}
ids <- c("(Intercept)", "X714", "X786", "X158", "X1027")
s <- summary(model)$coefficients[ids, ]
ci <- confint(model)[ids, ]
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Player = c("home court", "Durant", "Westbrook", "Nelson", "Benson"),
    Estimate = round(s[, "Estimate"], 3),
    SE = round(s[, "Std. Error"], 3),
    Low = round(ci[, 1], 3),
    High = round(ci[, 2], 3),
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  format = "simple",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

Low and High are the 95% interval: roughly Estimate \(\pm 2 \times\) SE.

## How to read the coefficients

* **Estimate**: expected change in home `PM` if that player is on the home five (`X = 1`) instead of sitting (`X = 0`)
* **Positive** Estimate: he helps the home margin. **Negative**: he hurts it
* If he is away (`X = -1`), predicted `PM` moves by **minus** the Estimate
* **(Intercept)**: home-court baseline, about \(0.09\) points per stint
* **Low to High**: plausible values of that effect. If **0 is inside** the range, we cannot tell this player from sitting
* Durant \(0.08\), range \(-0.49\) to \(0.65\): includes 0, so the point guess is not usable yet
* Benson \(2.12\), range \(-0.20\) to \(4.44\): first on the leaderboard, but the interval is huge (about 9 minutes)
* Home court \(0.05\) to \(0.13\): does not include 0, so that effect is the one we can actually see

## The first leaderboard

Do you know these players? These are \(\beta\) from the unfiltered model, largest first.

```{r}
coeff_all[names(coeff_all) != "(Intercept)"][1:10]
```

## What is wrong with this list?

```{r}
nba12p %>%
  filter(PlayerTrueName == "Benson, Keith") %>%
  select(PlayerTrueName, PlayerTeams, SimpleMin)
```

* Keith Benson played about 9 minutes for Golden State
* One lucky stint can put a player first
* With no minutes floor, the model believes a tiny sample

Rosenbaum keeps players above 250 minutes. A lower cutoff lets the lucky stint back in. A higher cutoff drops real rotation players.

## Minutes in this file

`SimpleMin` in `nba12p` is minutes in these stints. Rosenbaum keeps players above 250.

```{r}
summary(nba12p$SimpleMin)
```

## Minutes in this file

Most of the mass is rotation players. The left tail is the Bensons.

```{r, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7, fig.height=3.1, out.width="\\linewidth", fig.align="center"}
ggplot(nba12p, aes(SimpleMin)) +
  geom_histogram() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 250) +
  labs(title = "Minutes in this file", x = "SimpleMin", y = "Players")
```

## Players above 250 minutes

Keep those IDs from `nba12p`. Benson (about 9 minutes) will not be here.

\tiny
```{r}
more250 <- nba12p$PlayerID[nba12p$SimpleMin > 250]
length(more250)
nba12p %>%
  filter(PlayerID %in% more250) %>%
  select(PlayerID, PlayerTrueName, SimpleMin) %>%
  slice(1:4)
"Benson, Keith" %in% nba12p$PlayerTrueName[nba12p$SimpleMin > 250]
```

## Strip the `X` from column names

`nba5` columns are `X714`. `more250` is `714`. Strip the `X` so they match.

\tiny
```{r}
head(colnames(nba5), 4)
colnames(nba5) <- sub("^X", "", colnames(nba5))
head(colnames(nba5), 4)
```

`PM` is unchanged. Player columns are now the same strings as `PlayerID`.

## Keep those columns

Outcome plus the 250-minute players only. `check.names = FALSE` stops `data.frame()` from putting the `X` back on `714`.

\tiny
```{r}
nba6 <- data.frame(
  PM = nba5$PM,
  nba5[, colnames(nba5) %in% as.character(more250), drop = FALSE],
  check.names = FALSE
)
c(stints = nrow(nba6), players = ncol(nba6) - 1)
head(colnames(nba6), 5)
```

## Refit, 250-minute players

Same `lm(PM ~ .)`, fewer columns. Nelson is no longer sitting next to Benson.

\tiny
```{r}
model2 <- lm(PM ~ ., data = nba6)
coeff2 <- sort(coefficients(model2), decreasing = TRUE)
coeff_250 <- name_coeffs(coeff2, nba12p)
coeff_250[names(coeff_250) != "(Intercept)"][1:10]
```

Nelson, Jameer: [https://goo.gl/eNj7sq](https://goo.gl/eNj7sq)

## Where is Durant? Where is LeBron?

Rank among the 250-minute players. Still points per stint, not per possession.

```{r}
rbind(
  apm_rank(coeff_250, "Durant, Kevin"),
  apm_rank(coeff_250, "James, LeBron")
)
```

## Two stints are not the same length

Christmas, OKC: 18-18 in 12 and 13 possessions. A later 2-0 in one trip is a different rate. Next we divide.

\bcenter
\(\displaystyle \text{Margin} = \frac{\text{Home Points}}{\text{Home Possessions}} - \frac{\text{Away Points}}{\text{Away Possessions}}\)
\ecenter

## Points per possession

Same scoring and possession columns as in `nba12`.

\tiny
```{r}
nba12$Margin <- nba12$PointsScoredHome / nba12$PossessionsHome -
  nba12$PointsScoredAway / nba12$PossessionsAway
nba12 %>%
  filter(GameID == "20111225ORLOKC") %>%
  select(PointsScoredHome, PointsScoredAway,
         PossessionsHome, PossessionsAway, Margin) %>%
  slice(1:3)
```

First stint 18-18 on 12 and 13 trips: raw `PM` is 0, the rate is about 0.12.

## Zero possessions

`Margin` is home points per possession minus away points per possession. New York has 0 home possessions, so the first fraction is \(0/0\).

\tiny
```{r}
nba12 %>%
  filter(GameID == "20111225BOSNYK", PossessionsHome == 0) %>%
  select(PointsScoredHome, PointsScoredAway,
         PossessionsHome, PossessionsAway, Margin) %>%
  slice(1:3)
```

In R, \(0/0 =\) `NaN`. Then `NaN - 2` is still `NaN`. `lm` cannot use that row. Next slide drops it with `is.finite()`.

## Drop non-finite rows

`nba6` rows still line up with `nba12`. Replace raw `PM` with the rate, then keep finite rows only.

\tiny
```{r}
nba6$PM <- nba12$Margin
nba7 <- nba6[is.finite(nba6$PM), ]
c(before = nrow(nba6), after = nrow(nba7))
```

`Secs` is not a player. Add it only as a weight, later.

## Per-possession regression

Same 250-minute players. `PM` is now points per possession.

\tiny
```{r}
model3 <- lm(PM ~ ., data = nba7)
coeff3 <- sort(coefficients(model3), decreasing = TRUE)
coeff_poss <- name_coeffs(coeff3, nba12p)
coeff3 <- coeff_poss
```

## Per-possession leaderboard

Units changed. Nash at about 0.35 means four average teammates plus Nash score about 0.35 points per possession more than five average players.

```{r}
coeff3[names(coeff3) != "(Intercept)"][1:10]
```

Steve Nash, Phoenix: [https://goo.gl/BczeBv](https://goo.gl/BczeBv)

## Where is Durant? Where is LeBron?

Same rank helper, new units.

```{r}
rbind(
  apm_rank(coeff3, "Durant, Kevin"),
  apm_rank(coeff3, "James, LeBron")
)
```

## Durant and LeBron, four numbers

Same two players. The columns are not in the same units, so do not subtract them.

* Season plus/minus: a point total over the stints in this file
* Unfiltered and 250-minute: points per stint
* Per possession: points per possession

```{r, echo=FALSE}
pull_pm <- function(x, who) {
  hit <- unname(x[names(x) == who])
  if (length(hit) == 0) NA_real_ else hit[[1]]
}
compare <- data.frame(
  Player = c("Durant", "LeBron"),
  SeasonPM = c(durant_season, lebron_season),
  Unfiltered = c(pull_pm(coeff_all, "Durant, Kevin"), pull_pm(coeff_all, "James, LeBron")),
  Min250 = c(pull_pm(coeff_250, "Durant, Kevin"), pull_pm(coeff_250, "James, LeBron")),
  PerPoss = round(c(pull_pm(coeff_poss, "Durant, Kevin"), pull_pm(coeff_poss, "James, LeBron")), 3)
)
compare
```

## Center the coefficients

Subtract the mean. Then \(0\) is the average player in this model: positive is better than average, negative is worse.

```{r}
coeff3 <- coeff3 - mean(coeff3)
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, fig.width=7, fig.height=3.1, out.width="\\linewidth", fig.align="center"}
ggplot() + aes(coeff3) +
  geom_histogram() +
  labs(title = "Scaled per-possession coefficients", x = "APM", y = "Players")
```

## Other weights you could use

* Duration: a two-minute stint should count more than six seconds
* Clutch: 4th quarter or OT, under five minutes, lead inside \(X\) points
* Garbage time: 4th quarter or OT, lead larger than \(X\)

\(X\) is often 5 or 10. Next we weight by duration only.

# Weighted regression

## Stint length is not equal

`ElapsedSecs` is already in `nba12`. Christmas first stint is 364 seconds. A 6-second stint is in the same file.

\tiny
```{r}
nba12 %>%
  filter(GameID == "20111225ORLOKC") %>%
  select(ElapsedSecs, PointsScoredHome, PointsScoredAway, Margin) %>%
  slice(1:3)
```

## Weight by minutes

`nba7` rows are the finite-`Margin` rows of `nba12`, in the same order. `Secs` is a **weight**, not a player column, so it stays out of `lm`.

\tiny
```{r}
w <- nba12$ElapsedSecs[is.finite(nba12$Margin)] / 60
c(weights = length(w), rows = nrow(nba7))
model4 <- lm(PM ~ ., data = nba7, weights = w)
coeff4 <- name_coeffs(sort(coefficients(model4), decreasing = TRUE), nba12p)
coeff4[names(coeff4) != "(Intercept)"][1:10]
```

## APM is help, not a talent ranking

* APM is not a claim about how good or bad the player is as a person or as a scorer
* It is how much he moved the team's margin, given who else was on the floor

## APM regressed against other statistics

Dan Rosenbaum suggests to run the following regression to understand the impact of the box score statistics on APM  

\bcenter
$Y = \beta_0 + \beta_1X_1 + \beta_2X_2 + ... + \beta_kX_k + \epsilon$
\ecenter

Where Y is the coefficients of the players from Plus/Minus model,  

$X_1,..X_k$ are box score statistics

Each coefficient is the effect of that box-score statistic on APM.

## APM regressed against other statistics

```{r, echo=F, out.height="0.78\\textheight", fig.align="center"}
knitr::include_graphics("./images/statistics.png")
```


## Other metrics

* Box-Score PM (Statistical Plus/Minus)- use Box-Score statistics for each stint of time of time for each player as inputs (steals, rebounds, offensive rating, etc)
* ESPN-Real Plus/Minus – is calculated by ESPN again using some sort of regression analysis.
* Offensive Plus/Minus and Defensive Plus/Minus
* Win shares: Contribution of each player into wins of the
team.
* VORP – Value Over Replacement Level

## Where to find the ratings?

Plus/Minus  

* Best lineup by plus/minus  
[https://stats.nba.com/lineups/traditional/](https://stats.nba.com/lineups/traditional/)  

* ESPN: Offensive Real Plus/Minus, Defensive real Plus/Minus, RPM and Wins share (from 2014)
[https://www.espn.com/nba/statistics/rpm/_/sort/RPM](https://www.espn.com/nba/statistics/rpm/_/sort/RPM)  

* Plus minus by player  
[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/d/duranke01/gamelog/2012/](https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/d/duranke01/gamelog/2012/)


## Other Metrics

* WINVAL by Wayne Winston: The exact method of calculating tha Adjusted P/M is not public, however.  

\bcenter
*Margin of victory = sum(Rating of all 5 home team players) - sum(Rating of all 5 away team players)*
\ecenter

# Check

## Five questions

* A stint ends 2-0 for the home team. What is the plus/minus of a home player? Of an away player?
* In the adjusted model, what does an away player get in that row: 1, -1, or 0?
* Why can a player with about 9 minutes finish first?
* Points and minutes move together. Is that skill, or time on the floor?
* Nash is about 0.35 points per possession above four average teammates. What does that claim, and what does it not claim?
